title: E0001: Opening tag position
plain_english: The PHP opening tag (`<?php` or `<?=`) should be on the first line of the file, starting at column 1.
why_matters: If there is any whitespace, blank lines, or output before `<?php`, PHP may send headers and output to the browser earlier than expected. This can cause unexpected whitespace in JSON or API responses, "Headers already sent" warnings, or broken redirects and cookies.
bad_example:
<?php
// There is an empty blank line before the opening tag.
echo "Hello World";
what_it_checks: The PHP opening tag is on line 1.
The opening tag starts at column 1 (no leading indentation or spaces).
CLI scripts may use a Unix shebang (`#!...`) on line 1 before the opening tag.
